result.summary: Our patch adds a `checkLogPath` guard invoked before every log-serving command (GET_LOG_BYTES, VIEW_WHOLE_LOG, ROLL_VIEW_LOG, REMOVE_TASK_LOG) in the same dispatcher class the official fix touches, and it neutralizes the observed POV (`/etc/passwd` has no `.log` suffix, so it is rejected). However it is strictly weaker than the official fix: it validates only `!path.contains("..")` + `endsWith(".log")` and, critically, omits the official fix's base-directory anchoring (`path.startsWith(dsHome)`). As a result an attacker can still read any `.log` file anywhere on the filesystem, so the path-traversal/arbitrary-file-read class is not fully closed. The mechanism is a blocklist+suffix filter rather than canonicalize-and-contain, the CWE-022 defense-of-record.
result.root_cause: Untrusted, attacker-controlled `path` from ViewLog/GetLog/RollView/RemoveTask commands flows unchecked into file reads in LoggerUtils/LoggerRequestProcessor, allowing arbitrary file access; a correct fix must constrain the resolved path to the log base directory.

issues.description: Missing base-directory containment: unlike the official fix (path.startsWith(DOLPHINSCHEDULER_HOME)), our checkLogPath permits any absolute path ending in .log, so an attacker can still read arbitrary .log files anywhere on the filesystem — the arbitrary-file-read class is not fully closed.
Uses a blocklist ('..') plus suffix allowlist rather than canonicalize-then-verify-inside-base-dir; symlinks are not resolved, so a symlinked *.log could escape any intended directory.
Throws IllegalArgumentException whereas the official checkPathSecurity returns a boolean; callers relying on graceful boolean handling see a different control flow (minor divergence).
